# An online cart for the shop

## Table of Contents

- [Executive summary](#executive-summary) — what, for whom, why now
- [Problem](#problem) — phone orders
- [Solution](#solution) — a cart with trusted totals
- [What makes it different](#what-makes-it-different) — one pricing source
- [Who it serves](#who-it-serves) — regular shoppers
- [Success criteria](#success-criteria) — online orders
- [Scope](#scope) — cart and checkout only

## Executive summary

Regular shoppers want to order without phoning. An online cart whose total always matches what the shop charges lets them do it, and frees staff from keying orders.

## Problem

Shoppers phone in orders during opening hours only; staff key every order, and a busy line loses sales.

## Solution

A web cart where a shopper adds products, sees the total the shop will charge and checks out.

## What makes it different

Every total comes from the shop's own pricing source, so the online price is never a surprise.

## Who it serves

Regular shoppers who already order by phone, most of them on their phones.

## Success criteria

Online orders replace half the phone orders within six months.

## Scope

The cart and checkout. Search and saved items come later.
